+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M3MN916AA5AE3QAWE96S67KS
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '9780'
+title: 'OTel 3: swift-log records for agent run start, end and failure'
+---
+## Why
+Design of 2026-09-28 (item B and items 2 and 4): logs use `Logging.Logger` (swift-log), never `os.Logger`. A log message and its metadata never carry content.
+
+## What
+- One `Logging.Logger` with the label from `AgentsTelemetry` (task ^96s67ks), held by the runner or the run (`Run/AgentRunner.swift`, `Run/AgentRun.swift`). A host can pass its own `Logger`; the default is `Logger(label:)` from the vocabulary. Do not bootstrap `LoggingSystem` in the library.
+- Records, each with the metadata keys from `AgentsTelemetry` (agent name, run id, parent run id, caller session id, depth, outcome) and no content:
+  - run started (`.info`);
+  - run finished (`.info`), with the duration;
+  - run failed (`.error`), with the failure kind (hitMaxTurns, error, stopped, catalogNotLoaded, setup failure) and the error type name only; no error message text if it can hold model or tool content;
+  - run cancelled (`.info`).
+- The "enter" record of task ^wprxwv2 is separate; do not write it two times.
+- Confirm that `Sources` has no `os.Logger`, `import os`, or `OSSignposter` (it has none now); add a guard test so none comes back.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] Each run writes one start record and one end record (finished, failed or cancelled) with the metadata above.
+- [ ] No log message or metadata value holds content (the content-safety test of ^96s67ks covers the logs).
+- [ ] A guard test fails if `Sources` uses `os.Logger`, `import os` or `OSSignposter`.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsAgentsTests/AgentRunLoggingTests.swift` (new): a test log handler (injected, not a global bootstrap that other tests see) records the records of a finished, a failed (maxTurns) and a cancelled scripted run.
+- [ ] Add the `os` guard to the existing guard tests (`Tests/FoundationModelsAgentsTests/` guard suite).
+- [ ] Run `swift test -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors`. Expected: pass.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #otel
\ No newline at end of file

+  text: |-
+    Picked up. Research results (2026-09-29):
+    - `TelemetryCapture.Context.logger` (Extras `TelemetryTestSupport`) is a `Logger` whose handler writes to the capture of that context. It is a value, thus it keeps its handler on each task, also on the detached Router pump. A test gives it to the new seam; no test calls `LoggingSystem.bootstrap`.
+    - Plan: `AgentEnvironment.logger: Logger?` (default `nil`). Each run makes its logger when it starts: the logger of the environment, or `Logger(label: AgentsTelemetry.logLabel)`. +    - Records: start (`.info`); finished, cancelled (`.info`); failed (`.error`) with the failure kind and the error type name (`String(describing: type(of:))`), never the text of the failure. Each end record has the outcome and the duration.
+    - Failure kinds: add `setupFailed` (bodyRenderFailed, skillRenderFailed, agentsMdUnreadable, toolsFailed) and `catalogNotLoaded` to `AgentsTelemetry.FailureKind`. The span of a setup failure then has `setupFailed`, not `error`. `AgentRunner.start(_:prompt:)` writes one failed record with `catalogNotLoaded` when the catalog is not loaded; no run exists then, thus that record has no run id and no start record.
+    - Guard: a new guard suite scans `Sources` for `import os`, `os.Logger` and `OSSignposter`. `Sources` has none now.
